tasks.t: Write and approve an incident response plan (NIST 800-171 control 3.6.1)
tasks.why: You cannot meet a 72-hour deadline with no plan. This is also a 5-point control.

tasks.t: Name your incident response team and their roles
tasks.why: Who declares an incident, who contains it, who talks to DoD. Write names, not job titles.

tasks.t: Get access to the DoD DIBNet portal (dibnet.dod.mil)
tasks.why: This is where you file the report. Do not discover the login process during an incident.

tasks.t: List which of your contracts involve CUI and carry DFARS 252.204-7012
tasks.why: The 72-hour obligation only applies where the clause applies. Know where it applies now.

tasks.t: Document your notification chain: leadership, legal, prime (if you are a sub), contracting officer
tasks.why: Reporting to DoD is not your only notification. Your subcontracts and prime agreements add more.

tasks.t: Confirm you can preserve forensic images and logs without destroying evidence
tasks.why: DFARS 7012 requires you to preserve and protect images and system access for DoD review.

tasks.t: Run a tabletop exercise and record the after-action notes
tasks.why: The first time your team practices should not be the first real incident.

phases.title: Prepare now (before anything happens)
phases.window: Do this before you ever need it

tasks.t: Record the exact date and time of discovery
tasks.why: The 72-hour clock starts here. Write it down immediately.

tasks.t: Activate the incident response team
tasks.why: Follow the plan, not improvisation.

tasks.t: Isolate affected systems; stop the bleeding
tasks.why: Disconnect, do not power off. Memory and logs vanish on shutdown.

tasks.t: Preserve forensic images and logs
tasks.why: DFARS 7012 requires preservation for DoD. Copy first, analyze second.

tasks.t: Do not destroy, alter, or reimage anything yet
tasks.why: Destroyed evidence cannot be recovered, and DoD may ask for it.

tasks.t: Open an incident log and timestamp every action
tasks.why: Your log becomes the backbone of the DoD report.

tasks.t: Determine which systems and data are affected
tasks.why: You must know whether CUI was involved before you file.

tasks.t: Identify the CUI categories and contracts touched
tasks.why: The report requires affected contract numbers and CUI impact.

tasks.t: Collect indicators of compromise and preserve malware samples
tasks.why: DoD may request malicious software submission after your report.

tasks.t: Engage forensic support if the team cannot scope it alone
tasks.why: A wrong scope statement in a federal report is worse than a slow one.

tasks.t: Brief leadership and legal counsel
tasks.why: Legal privilege and disclosure decisions happen here, not in the portal form.

tasks.t: Draft the incident report with all required fields
tasks.why: See the report guide below for the full field list.

tasks.t: Submit the report via the DIBNet portal before hour 72
tasks.why: Late is noncompliant. Aim for hour 48, not hour 71.

tasks.t: Notify your prime contractor (if you are a subcontractor)
tasks.why: Your prime has its own reporting obligations up the chain.

tasks.t: Notify the contracting officer as your contract requires
tasks.why: The portal report and the contracting officer notice are separate duties.

tasks.t: Save the submission confirmation and report number
tasks.why: Proof of timely filing lives in your records.

phases.title: Hours 24 to 72: Report
phases.window: File before the deadline, not at it

tasks.t: Submit malicious software to DoD when requested
tasks.why: DFARS 7012 requires submission upon DoD request after your report.

tasks.t: Cooperate with DoD follow-up and preserve access as required
tasks.why: Preservation obligations continue past the initial report.

tasks.t: Provide updated reports as the investigation concludes
tasks.why: Initial reports are preliminary by nature. Update the record.

tasks.t: Run a lessons-learned review and record it
tasks.why: Feed findings back into controls 3.6.1 and your SSP.

tasks.t: Update your SSP and POA&M with corrective actions
tasks.why: The incident exposed a gap. Document the fix or it will recur.

phases.title: After 72 hours: Follow through
phases.window: The report is the middle, not the end

report_fields.d: Legal name, CAGE/UEI, and who DoD can reach
Every contract whose CUI or systems are involved
What happened, in factual terms, no speculation
When it happened and when you found it
Which systems, which CUI categories, estimated scope
What the incident did or could do to covered defense information
What you have done and what remains
Note whether malware was found and preserved for submission
